notes.title: First Two Days of Script Translated into Japanese & Chinese!
notes.notes: [p]I’d like to express my deepest gratitude to our volunteer translators — [b]Kandze Cheng, Rintaro Kanaki, and Taiga Murakami[/b]. Thanks to their incredible work, the first two days of the script have already been translated into Japanese and Chinese.[/p][p]This is a huge step forward for the project. If I had commissioned a professional translation, just the first day alone would have cost around $1000–2000 for both languages. Now, those saved resources can be directed into other crucial areas of development — graphics, music, and overall atmosphere of [i]“Cycle of Struggle: Ardengrad”[/i].[/p][p]A very special thank you also goes to [b]Vanya (aka Obakasan)[/b]. Without his help as a mediator and coordinator, this translation simply wouldn’t have happened. He turned an idea into reality.[/p][p]For an indie project, this kind of support is truly priceless. I’m genuinely happy to see a community forming around the game, with people willing to contribute their time, energy, and talent.[/p][p]Thank you, Kandze, Rintaro, Taiga, and Vanya! ❤️[/p]

notes.title: Act I is complete — 32,800 words ready for production!
notes.notes:
[p][b]Act I is complete — 32,800 words ready for production![/b][/p][p]We've finished work on the final version of Act I's script. 32,800 words: vivid dialogues, choices, polylogues, monologues, scenes of pain and warmth—all proofread, polished, and ready to be brought into the engine.[/p][p]That means one thing: pre-production is over. Officially.[/p][p]Next comes the first build. The characters are gaining voice and form. Their stories are becoming interactive, and the world they live in—closer, sharper, more alive.
Yura, Yesya, Dima, Katya, Anya, Masha, and Nadya—no longer just names on paper. Now, they’re part of the game.[/p][p]Thank you to everyone who's been with us—who waited, who believed, who asked the hard questions.
The best is yet to come.[/p]

notes.notes: Refined the text: minor typo fixes and improved phrasing for smoother dialogue flow. Thanks to everyone who shares their feedback!
